module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Paths
public import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
public import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- A family of paths covering all vertices without overlaps. -/
def IsPathCover (G : SimpleGraph α) (P : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
  (∀ s1 ∈ P, ∀ s2 ∈ P, s1 ≠ s2 → Disjoint s1 s2) ∧
  (Finset.univ ⊆ P.biUnion id) ∧
  (∀ s ∈ P, ∃ (u v : α) (p : G.Walk u v), p.IsPath ∧ s = p.support.toFinset)

/-- Minimum size of a path cover of `G`. -/
noncomputable def pathCoverNumber (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℕ :=
  sInf { k | ∃ P : Finset (Finset α), P.card = k ∧ IsPathCover G P }

end SimpleGraph

reformulations.difference: The family is represented by finite vertex sets with existential path witnesses, rather than by chosen path objects. Coverage is written as inclusion of Finset.univ in the union.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Each witness is a walk with no repeated vertices, and its support is nonempty, including for a length-zero path. Pairwise disjointness and coverage therefore partition the vertex type into path supports. Choosing one path per block gives an actual vertex-disjoint path cover with exactly P.card paths. Conversely, the supports of vertex-disjoint paths are distinct because they are nonempty, so passing to their finite set preserves the number of paths. The union cannot contain anything outside Finset.univ, making the inclusion exact coverage. Review.cover_iff_unique_partition and Review.cover_iff_chosen_paths in scratch.lean prove these characterizations.

reformulations.difference: The minimum is expressed using the natural-number infimum of realized cover cardinalities.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite graph has a cover consisting of all singleton vertex sets, witnessed by length-zero paths. Thus the defining set of cardinalities is always nonempty, even for an empty vertex type. Nat.sInf_mem and Nat.sInf_le make its infimum an attained minimum, not an empty-set default. Review.number_eq_iff proves that pathCoverNumber G = k is equivalent to existence of a k-element cover together with k being no larger than every cover cardinality.

review.notes: Both definitions and their sole problem consumer, WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture40.conjecture40, were checked. The primary-source glossary defines p(G) as “The minimum number of vertex disjoint paths needed to cover the vertices of the graph.” It does not require induced paths. Conjecture 40's formula, nontrivial connected-graph hypotheses, and open-status marker agree with the Lean file. No existing Mathlib path-cover definition was found. The scratch file compiles successfully, and its checked proofs have no sorryAx dependency. Tests establish that the minimum is attained, it is zero exactly for an empty vertex type, the edgeless graph has cover number equal to its vertex count, and K₃ has cover number one. Computational tests also reject overlapping blocks, uncovered vertices, and empty blocks. Experiments are in /workspace/review/; no repository files were modified.
